sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Middelburg, the capital of Zeeland, charges for street parking in a yellow zone around the centre and has made the street progressively dearer than its garages. Since 1 June 2025 the street tariff replaced the former two-hour maximum stay with 3 euros an hour for the first two hours and 6 euros from the third, to discourage long stays in the centre [4]. The 2026 regulation, decided by the council on 18 December 2025, sets 3.20 euros an hour for the first two hours and 6.40 euros from the third in the yellow zone, and 3.20 euros for the first four hours and 6.40 afterwards on the Damplein [0]. The car parks Hof van Tange, Loskade and Molenwater cost 3.20 euros an hour or 16.00 euros a day, about 7 percent more than in 2025 [1]. Paid parking runs Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 20:00, with no Sunday charging [2]. A first resident permit costs 8.70 euros a month and a second 28.80 euros, and a business permit 26.10 euros a month [3]. The municipality's amended draft parking policy of 1 July 2025, a proposal for which no adoption is shown, steers towards a car-light centre with residential streets reserved for residents, their visitors and business permit holders. Its advised first step would extend regulation from the present hours to 06:00-24:00, seven days a week, but only once new edge parking has been realised [10]. A consultation on it drew 100 written responses, and the report stresses that no location for expansion had been chosen [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The question is where to put extra edge parking. The draft report names the NS station park-and-ride site, owned by NS Vastgoed, and Oude Veerseweg as the most likely sites, with indicative extra capacity of 360 and 300 spaces; a council amendment of 30 January 2025 added Hof van Tange to the study with 120, described as complex because of its heritage value, and no site had been chosen [11]. Its rough estimates are 6 million euros for the station site, 13 million for Oude Veerseweg and 15 million for Hof van Tange, with 3 to 5 years from research to completion and no bus-served transferium advised [12]. On charging, traffic decisions reserved bays at 28 locations in December 2021, 16 in February 2024 and 17 in December 2024, including the Molenwater car park, which are designations of bays and not proof of working chargers [16]. A press report says the garage tariff would not change with the progressive street tariff and that a scan car would check parking from May 2025 [5].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality itself operates the garages, with a parking management system and tariffs set in the municipal table [15]. The 2025 report describes four public garages, Geere, Kousteensedijk, Achter de Houttuinen and Kanaalweg, with about 1,000 spaces, about 3,200 on-street spaces inside the Vesten and a free car park of about 230 spaces at Oude Veerseweg [7]. It puts the garage tariff at 2.30 euros an hour against 3.00 on the street, at 2024 prices, and says the garages are deliberately cheaper to pull visitors off the street; we confirmed no 2026 garage tariff [6]. Counts by an advisory firm in August and October 2023 found hardly any spare capacity, an overloaded Oude Veerseweg and a peak on Saturday afternoons [8], and the report says the existing guidance system sends visitors away from full garages and is to be reviewed [9]. Q-Park lists the P+R Segeersingel at the station with 240 spaces, open round the clock, with a discount for rail travellers; its tariff did not load [14].

Our data cover that park-and-ride, whose feed gives 182 spaces against Q-Park's 240, so the percentages are approximate. Over about 61 days since 22 August 2026 occupancy averaged about 35% on weekdays and 25% at weekends, and it reached full in a single reading on a Thursday around midday. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
